simple.inThisVerse: The selected word is tied to טִפְסַר (H2951) in the Hebrew source text. Part of speech: n-m.

simple.summary: טִפְסַר (ṭiphçar) means a military governor First listed occurrence: Jer 51 27.

definitions.full: H2951. tiphsar טִפְסָר noun [masculine] scribe, marshal (if meaning correct, then Assyrian loan-word, from dupsarru, tablet-writer, scribe , see Len Langue Primit. de la Chaldeve, 365 Schr COT on Jer 51:27 , Lotz TP 180 ; dupšarru , according to Dl HWB 227 ) — plural suffix טַפְסְרַיִךְ Nahum 3:17 (as if from טַפְסֵר ) thy scribes, marshals , of high officials of Nineveh; absolute singular טִפְסָר עָלֶיהָ מִּקְדוּ Jer 51:27 appoint a marshal against her , i.e. against Babylon. — On military function of those skilled in writing compare שֹׁטֵר .
